key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within minutes to hours. Acute, dramatic presentation. LOCATION: Unilateral FLANK PAIN. RADIATES from flank→groin→testicle (males) or labia (females). Follows ureter path. DURATION: Waves last minutes, entire episode lasts hours. COLICKY (comes and goes in waves). CHARACTER: SEVERE COLICKY PAIN described as SHARP, STABBING, or 'WORST PAIN OF MY LIFE'. Intensity waxes and wanes. AGGRAVATING: NOTHING specifically worsens (spontaneous waves). Movement doesn't change intensity. Dehydration may precipitate. RELIEVING: NOTHING relieves during wave. Position changes don't help (patient RESTLESS, paces, cannot find comfort - unlike peritonitis where still). Narcotics needed. TIMING: COMES IN WAVES - intense for minutes, then slightly better, then intense again. Pattern repeats. Not constant. SEVERITY: 8-10/10, extremely severe and dramatic. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: NAUSEA AND VOMITING (very common), HEMATURIA (blood in urine - 90%, gross or microscopic), urinary frequency, urgency. KEY POSITIVES: CVA tenderness, hematuria, colicky waves, restlessness, flank→groin radiation. KEY NEGATIVES: Peritoneal signs (rigidity) suggest alternative. FEVER suggests pyelonephritis not stone. Bilateral pain unusual.

red_flags: Fever with flank pain - infected stone (pyonephrosis), needs urgent urology intervention
Anuria (no urine output) - complete obstruction, needs urgent decompression
Single kidney with obstructing stone - urgent urology consult
Severe pain unresponsive to narcotics - may need urgent intervention
